theater: 關中涇原奉天靈台一線

battle.name: 奉天、靈台之戰
battle.theater: 關中涇原奉天靈台一線
battle.brief: 永泰元年（765）九月，叛將僕固懷恩勾結吐蕃、回紇、党項羌，率三十餘萬眾三路南下，進逼長安。唐廷分兵扼守東渭橋、雲陽與奉天、邠州，渾瑊守奉天出奇兵夜襲蕃營；郭子儀遣李光瓚說反回紇，十月十五日靈台西原大破尚結息部，聯軍退走。卡面的羅馬弩砲不在此役現場，僅作同族投射兵器之對照。

kit.name: 羅馬弩砲
kit.history: 扭力弩砲，一發一具箭。羅馬用它拆掉希臘的城牆，也拆掉了希臘的城邦體系。

countries: 交戰的兩大陣營分屬唐與反唐聯軍。唐朝一方以中央禁軍六軍為骨幹，輔以各鎮節度使行營：淮西節度使李忠臣領兵駐東渭橋，檢校太子太保李光進率軍進雲陽，鎮西節度使馬璘與河南節度使郝庭玉屯便橋，鳳翔節度使李抱玉守鳳翔，同華節度使周智光守同州，鄜坊節度使杜晃屯坊州，軍容使駱奉先與將軍李日超守盩厔；前線另有朔方兵馬使渾瑊、討擊使白元光部守奉天，邠州守將白孝德閉城拒守，唐代宗本人親率六軍屯禁苑督戰。反唐聯軍則以叛唐的河北副元帥僕固懷恩為核心，他勾結吐蕃、回紇、党項羌、奴剌、吐谷渾等勢力，據《資治通鑑》說法聯軍總數記作三十餘萬，另有數十萬一說；其中回紇為繼吐蕃之後入寇者，僕固懷恩自領朔方兵二十萬為後援。吐蕃大將尚結息、贊摩、馬重英率北路主力，經涇州、邠州、鳳翔府攻取奉天（今陝西乾縣）、醴泉（今陝西禮泉北），直逼長安；党項帥任敷、鄭庭、郝德自東路攻同州（今陝西大荔），並限期自華陰取藍田，以扼南路；西路由吐谷渾、奴剌眾攻盩厔（今陝西周至）。戰場縱貫陝甘兩省涇原、關中一線，奉天在涇水之北的乾州之地，靈台在今甘肅靈台縣東南，涇陽則在今涇陽縣東南，三處構成聯軍由北而南壓境的骨架。
countriesEn: Two great coalitions faced each other: the Tang dynasty on one side, and an anti-Tang coalition on the other. The Tang fielded the imperial guard of the Six Armies (liu jun) as its backbone, reinforced by the armies of the regional jiedushi: the Huaixi jiedushi Li Zhongchen held the Eastern Weiqiao, the Lieutenant Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince Li Guangjin advanced to Yunyang, the Zhenxi jiedushi Ma Lin and Henan jiedushi Hao Tingyu garrisoned the Bian Bridge, the Fengxiang jiedushi Li Baoyu held Fengxiang, the Tonghua jiedushi Zhou Zhiguang held Tongzhou, the Fufang jiedushi Du Huang camped at Fangzhou, and the Military Commissioner Luo Fengxian together with General Li Richao guarded Zhizhi. On the front line, the Bingzhou Army Commander Hun Jian and the Chief of Volunteers for Expedition Bai Yuanguang defended Fengtian, while the governor of Binzhou, Bai Xiaode, shut the gates and refused to be drawn out. The Tang emperor himself camped at the Imperial Park with the Six Armies to supervise the fighting. The rebel coalition was built around Pugu Huai'en, the former Vice Commander-in-Chief of Hebei, who had gone over to the Tibetans and allied himself with the Tubo, the Uyghur, the Tangxiang, the Nulüe and the Tuyuhun. The Zizhi Tongjian records the coalition at a little over 300,000 men, with other sources saying several hundred thousand; the Uyghur came in after the Tibetans, and Pugu Huai'en himself led 200,000 Hebei troops as the rear guard. The northern column was commanded by the Tibetan generals Shang Jiexi, Zanmo and Ma Zhongying, who came through Jingzhou, Binzhou and Fengxiang prefecture to take Fengtian (today Qian county, Shaanxi) and Liquan (north of present-day Liquan, Shaanxi), pressing straight on Chang'an. On the eastern road, the Tangxiang commanders Ren Fu, Zheng Ting and Hao De struck Tongzhou (today Dali, Shaanxi) with orders to seize Lantian from Huayin by a set date and seal off the southern approach; on the western road, the Tuyuhun and Nulüe masses attacked Zhizhi (today Zhouzhi, Shaanxi). The battlefield ran along a line in Jingyuan and Guanzhong that straddles today's Shaanxi and Gansu: Fengtian lay in the Qianzhou country north of the Jing River, Lingtai lies southeast of present-day Lingtai county in Gansu, and Jingyang lies southeast of present-day Jingyang county. These three points formed the skeleton of the coalition's southward advance.
people: 唐代宗李豫是這場戰役的唐方最高決策者，他在形勢最緊時下制親征，把六軍屯於長安城北的禁苑，卻不輕易出城野戰，決策重心落在各節度使的守點與反擊上。僕固懷恩是整場戰役的軸心：他原為河北副元帥兼朔方重鎮，與宦官魚朝恩積怨、家族屢遭朝廷處置，遂聯絡吐蕃、回紇與邊地諸部舉兵，志在直取長安；史載其與唐廷之間早有嫌隙，河北軍中多部將與之響應，九月起兵後又自領朔方兵二十萬作後援，聯軍聲勢由此最盛。名將郭子儀是唐方真正扭轉戰局的人：五月出鎮河中，九月上書說明僕固懷恩騎兵不可輕敵、請各道節度使扼守衝要，戰事後期又利用吐蕃與回紇爭奪盟主之位的矛盾，遣牙將李光瓚游說回紇，並親自入回紇營與首領執酒定約，終使聯軍在出擊前先自相分裂。前線將領中，渾瑊以二百驍勇騎兵出其不意衝入蕃軍營陣、俘其將一員而己方無一傷亡，退回城後又夜襲敵營、殺千餘人，生擒五百人，是全役最突出的戰術奇襲；白元光以精騎追擊退兵之敵，於靈台西原一役中扮演先鋒。白孝德守邠州堅不出戰，拖住蕃軍數日；周智光於澄城北阻擊蕃軍得勝；馬璘派遊騎四百餘人於武功東原、又以五十名精兵偷襲蕃軍游騎得手。吐蕃方面，以尚結息為全軍主將，贊摩、馬重英分將其眾；回紇首領藥葛羅原本站在聯軍一邊，倒戈後成為追擊尚結息的主帥。
peopleEn: Emperor Daizong of Tang, Li Yu, was the supreme decision-maker on the Tang side. At the height of the crisis he issued an order for a personal campaign and quartered the Six Armies in the Imperial Park north of Chang'an, yet he rarely fought in the open, leaving the defence of strongpoints and the counterattack in the hands of the regional commanders. Pugu Huai'en was the axis of the entire campaign: formerly Vice Commander-in-Chief of Hebei and holder of a key military circuit, he had long been at odds with the eunuch Yu Chao'en and had seen his family repeatedly punished by the court, so he linked up with the Tibetans, the Uyghur and the various frontier peoples to raise troops with the aim of taking Chang'an outright. Historical records note that the rift between him and the court was of long standing, and that many officers in the Hebei armies answered his call; after he rose in September he further led 200,000 Hebei troops as the rear guard, which made the coalition at its most imposing. The famous general Guo Ziyi was the man who actually turned the battle. He took command at Hezhong in May, reported to the court in September that Pugu Huai'en's cavalry must not be treated lightly and that every circuit commander should be sent to hold the vital points, and in the later stages exploited the quarrel between the Tibetans and the Uyghur over who should lead the coalition, sending his subordinate Li Guangzhan to sound out the Uyghur and then going in person to the Uyghur camp, where he drank with their leader and sealed a pact. The alliance thus split before it could strike. Among the front-line commanders, Hun Jian was the most striking: he led two hundred picked cavalrymen straight into the Tibetan camp in a sudden stroke, taking their general prisoner with not a single man of his own lost, and after falling back into the city launched a night raid on the enemy camp, killing more than a thousand men and taking five hundred alive, the sharpest tactical stroke of the whole war. Bai Yuanguang led elite cavalry in the pursuit of the retreating enemy and played the part of spearhead in the battle on the Lingtai western plain. Bai Xiaode held Binzhou without yielding and tied the Tibetans up for several days; Zhou Zhiguang intercepted them north of Chengcheng and won; Ma Lin posted some four hundred light cavalry on the eastern plain of Wugong and sent fifty picked men to surprise the Tibetan outriders successfully. On the Tibetan side, Shang Jiexi was the commander of the entire army, with Zanmo and Ma Zhongying leading parts of it; the Uyghur leader Yao Geluo had originally stood with the coalition, and after his defection he became the commander who pursued Shang Jiexi.
kits: 這張卡的兵器是羅馬弩砲（Scorpio），即以扭力絞弦發射粗重箭矢的單發投射器，羅馬人用它拆希臘城牆。必須說明：公元765年的關中戰場上沒有羅馬人，這件兵器本身並不在本役現場，它在此只代表同一類型的投射兵器，幫助讀者理解「攻城靠投射器、守城靠投射器」這個技術框架。真正出現在奉天、靈台前線的投射兵器分兩路：唐軍有弩砲與床弩這類固定或半固定的大型弩機，用以在遠距離壓制城頭、封鎖城門通道，另有拋石機、飛石機一類以配重或人力拋擲石塊的器械；吐蕃與回紇的攻城裝備同樣齊備，《資治通鑑》記兩軍在奉天、醴泉、涇陽、靈台一線反覆攻守，戰後唐軍於奉天、涇陽連營繳獲「器械、軍旗共三萬餘件」，反映雙方隨軍的帳幕、旗幟、攻城器具與繩索器材數量驚人，其中必然包含攻城的投射器具，但史籍只概稱「器械」，不細列器種，故此不宜斷言某一具就是弩砲。除投射器外，決定本役勝負的裝備是馬匹與輕騎裝備：吐蕃、回紇、党項羌皆有大量騎兵，奉天城下渾瑊以二百騎出擊、白元光以精騎追擊、馬璘以四百遊騎巡野，都建立在唐代軍馬與騎兵武器的供應上；唐軍此役繳獲馬一千二百四十二匹、駝一百一十五頭，可見聯軍的隊伍中大量依靠駱駝馱載給養與器械，機動與補給高度依賴畜力。輕裝遠射的弓弩、標槍、環首刀與皮甲，是雙方步卒的常備；唐軍的禁軍六軍、節度使行營則按唐制配發制式武裝與旗鼓儀仗，是當時中央軍的標準配備。
kitsEn: The weapon on this card is the Roman Scorpio, a single-shot torsion-powered thrower that fired heavy bolts and was used by the Romans to breach Greek city walls. It must be said plainly: no Romans were on the Guanzhong battlefield in the year 765, and the weapon itself was not present in this campaign. It stands here only as a representative of the same family of missile weapons, to help the reader grasp the technical frame in which both besiegers and besieged relied on projectile artillery. The actual missile weapons on the Fengtian and Lingtai front fell into two camps. The Tang had large crossbow-throwers and bed-mounted crossbows of a fixed or semi-fixed type, used to keep long-range pressure on the parapets and to seal the approaches to city gates, together with counterweight and hand-powered stone-throwers. The Tibetan and Uyghur besiegers were equally well equipped for siege. The Zizhi Tongjian records that the two sides fought and besieged each other repeatedly along the line of Fengtian, Liquan, Jingyang and Lingtai, and that after the fighting the Tang army at Fengtian and Jingyang seized no fewer than thirty thousand items of equipment and military flags, which shows how enormous the train of tents, standards, siege apparatus and rigging was on both sides. That haul must have included siege projectiles, but the historical record only says 'equipment' in general and does not itemise the types, so it would be wrong to claim that any particular machine among them was a scorpio. Beyond the artillery, the equipment that decided this campaign was horses and light cavalry gear. The Tibetans, Uyghur and Tangxiang all fielded large numbers of mounted men: the two hundred riders Hun Jian took out against Fengtian, the elite cavalry Bai Yuanguang sent in pursuit, and the four hundred light horse Ma Lin ranged over the Wugong plain all rested on the Tang warhorse and mounted armament supply. In this campaign the Tang recovered 1,242 horses and 115 camels, showing how heavily the coalition relied on pack camels to carry rations and materiel, so that mobility and supply were bound up with animal power. Bows and crossbows, javelins, ring-pommel sabres and leather armour were the standard kit of infantry on both sides, while the imperial Six Armies and the circuit armies were issued arms and the drums and standards of Tang regulation as the standard equipment of the central army.
tactics: 聯軍的戰術骨架是三路鉗形，目標是合圍長安而非攻下一座城：北路吐蕃與回紇主力沿涇州、邠州、鳳翔南下，先以「攻數日不下」的硬攻試探唐軍城防，轉而取奉天、醴泉這些關中北緣的縣城作屯駐點，企圖藉地緣逼近長安；東路党項自同州方向猛攻，限期取華陰、藍田，斷絕關中與河東的聯絡；西路吐谷渾、奴剌攻盩厔，牽制唐廷從西南方向抽兵的餘地；僕固懷恩自領朔方兵二十萬壓在最後，任一線得手即可長驅直入。唐廷的應對不是求戰，而是分守與消耗：各節度使被派往東渭橋、雲陽、便橋、鳳翔、同州、坊州這些橫亙關中的要點，構成一條自東向西的遲滯防線；邠州守將白孝德閉城拒守，以「攻數日不下」拖住北路蕃軍的銳氣與日程；唐廷同時派遊騎四處巡野，馬璘部在武功東原以五十精兵偷襲蕃軍游騎，是把「守」與「騷擾」結合的典型手段。攻守相持數日後，戰局由奇襲與外交兩條線扭轉：九月廿一日後蕃軍初至奉天列營，渾瑊即以二百驍勇騎兵不待其陣勢已成而直衝其營，俘將數十、己方零傷亡，退入城中；入夜再襲其營，殺千餘人、生擒五百、繳獲駝馬器械，使蕃軍無法安營。十月聯軍合兵再攻奉天、轉圍涇陽，郭子儀令守將嚴守不戰，聯軍傍晚退扎北原；初九僕固懷恩暴死的消息傳到，吐蕃與回紇為爭盟軍之主而失和、分營，郭子儀乘勢遣李光瓚游說並親赴回紇營執酒定約，回紇轉而倒戈追擊尚結息，白元光率精騎增援，於十月十五日在靈台西原追上尚未結陣的吐蕃十萬餘人而大破之，十月十八日唐與回紇再於涇州東部合擊，終使吐蕃主將中箭退兵。整體而言，唐方以分守、遊騎、夜襲拖延消耗聯軍，再用游說分化敵營，最後以聯軍追擊之勢完成殲滅性的靈台西原攻擊，節奏全由唐方控制。
tacticsEn: The tactical skeleton of the coalition was a three-pronged pincer aimed at encircling Chang'an rather than storming a single city. The northern Tibetans and Uyghur came down through Jingzhou, Binzhou and Fengxiang prefecture, first testing the Tang defences with hard assaults that 'failed to take the city after several days', then seizing the county towns on the northern rim of Guanzhong such as Fengtian and Liquan as staging points in the hope that geography alone would carry them to Chang'an. The eastern Tangxiang pressed hard on Tongzhou, with a deadline to take Huayin and Lantian and cut the link between Guanzhong and Hedong. In the west the Tuyuhun and Nulüe struck Zhizhi, limiting the court's freedom to draw troops from the south-west. Pugu Huai'en trailed behind with 200,000 Hebei troops, ready to march straight into the capital the moment any one front broke through. The Tang answer was not to seek battle but to divide, hold and exhaust. Each jiedushi was posted to a key point strung across Guanzhong — the Eastern Weiqiao, Yunyang, the Bian Bridge, Fengxiang, Tongzhou, Fangzhou — forming a slow defensive line running east to west. The governor of Binzhou, Bai Xiaode, shut his gates and refused to be drawn out, using the fact that 'several days of assaulting produced no result' to bleed the northern Tibetans of momentum and time. At the same time the court sent light cavalry out to patrol the country: Ma Lin's detachment on the eastern plain of Wugong sent fifty picked men to surprise the Tibetan outriders, a typical way of combining defence with harassment. After several days of stalemate, the battle turned on two lines at once, surprise and diplomacy. After the Tibetans first took up position outside Fengtian, Hun Jian led two hundred picked cavalry straight into their camp before they could finish forming, taking their general and several dozen men with not one of his own lost, and fell back into the city; that night he raided the same camp, killing more than a thousand, taking five hundred alive and seizing camels, horses and equipment, so that the enemy could not settle in. In October the coalition regrouped and struck Fengtian again, then ringed Jingyang, but Guo Ziyi ordered the garrison to hold fast and not engage; the coalition withdrew at dusk to camp on the northern plain. On the ninth the news reached them that Pugu Huai'en had died suddenly, and the Tibetans and the Uyghur, quarrelling over who should lead the alliance, fell out and split into separate camps. Guo Ziyi seized the moment: he sent Li Guangzhan to make contact, went himself to the Uyghur camp and sealed a pact over wine, and the Uyghur turned and pursued Shang Jiexi, while Bai Yuanguang brought up elite cavalry to reinforce them. On the fifteenth of October they caught the Tibetan host of more than 100,000 men before it could form up and destroyed it on the western plain of Lingtai; on the eighteenth the Tang and Uyghur struck together again east of Jingzhou, until the Tibetan commander was shot in the arrow and the army broke. In sum, the Tang side fought by holding, harassing, raiding by night to delay and exhaust the coalition, then splitting the enemy camp by persuasion, and finally letting the coalition's own pursuit become the vehicle for the crushing blow on the Lingtai plain. The rhythm of the whole campaign was set by the Tang.
data: 《資治通鑑》卷二百二十三（唐紀三十九）是本役最核心的史料，其數字須分兩類看待。兵員方面：僕固懷恩勾結的聯軍總數記作三十餘萬，另有數十萬一說；其中回紇為繼吐蕃之後入寇，僕固懷恩自領朔方兵二十萬為後援；北路蕃軍攻奉天時以十萬眾至，宕昌之役中尚結息部亦稱十萬餘人；十月十五日靈台西原一役，唐軍大破尚結息十萬餘人。傷亡與繳獲：《資治通鑑》記唐蕃前後交戰二百餘次，唐軍殺傷蕃軍萬餘眾，斬殺五千人、生擒一百六十人，繳獲馬一千二百四十二匹、駝一百一十五頭，器械與軍旗共三萬餘件；奉天夜襲一役記殺千餘人、生擒五百人；十月十五日靈台西原一役記殺吐蕃將士五萬、生擒近萬人。這類斬首數在唐代史籍中普遍偏高，遠近難以核對，只能視為「宣稱戰果」而非實點，可靠的定性判斷是：吐蕃南路主力在此役遭到重創，十月十八日涇州東部再戰時主將中箭、軍心大亂而退，這一點由雙方記述一致。時間線清楚可考：九月二十一日唐廷下制親征，九月二十八日蕃軍北趨醴泉，十月初一退兵邠州與回紇合兵，初三再攻奉天，初八圍涇陽，初九僕固懷恩暴死，十五日靈台西原大捷，十八日涇州再勝，聯軍退出關中。戰役全歷約五十日，唐方以有限兵力在多處要點分兵抵抗，最終以一次追擊決戰定局。
dataEn: The Zizhi Tongjian, volume 223 (Tang Chronicle 39), is the core source for this campaign, and its figures fall into two different kinds that must be treated separately. On numbers of men: the coalition Pugu Huai'en assembled is recorded at a little over 300,000, with other sources saying several hundred thousand. The Uyghur came in after the Tibetans, and Pugu Huai'en led 200,000 Hebei troops as the rear guard. The northern Tibetans brought 100,000 men against Fengtian, and Shang Jiexi's column was likewise said to number more than 100,000 when it was caught on the western plain of Lingtai. On casualties and captures: the Tongjian records that Tang and Tibetan forces engaged more than two hundred times, that the Tang killed more than ten thousand of the enemy, cut down five thousand, took one hundred and sixty alive, and recovered 1,242 horses, 115 camels, and more than thirty thousand items of equipment and military flags. The night raid on Fengtian alone is credited with killing over a thousand and taking five hundred alive. The Lingtai plain battle of 15 October is credited with killing fifty thousand Tibetan soldiers and taking nearly ten thousand alive. Such head-count figures are notoriously inflated across Tang historical writing and cannot be checked at this distance; they should be read as claimed results rather than counted ones. The reliable qualitative judgement is that the Tibetan southern main force was badly mauled in this campaign, and that at the second engagement east of Jingzhou on 18 October the Tibetan commander was struck by an arrow and the army broke and withdrew — a point on which both sides' accounts agree. The chronology is clear and checkable: on the twenty-first day of the ninth month the Tang court ordered a personal campaign; on the twenty-eighth the Tibetans moved north towards Liquan; on the first day of the tenth month they withdrew to Binzhou and joined the Uyghur, and on the third they attacked Fengtian again; on the eighth they ringed Jingyang; on the ninth Pugu Huai'en died suddenly; on the fifteenth came the great victory on the Lingtai plain; on the eighteenth another victory at Jingzhou; and the coalition then left Guanzhong. The whole campaign lasted roughly fifty days, and the Tang side, with limited troops divided among several vital points, ultimately decided it with a single pursuing strike.
cause: 直接起因是安史之亂後的河北軍鎮與中央之間矛盾失調，以及唐廷對邊事的連串失誤。僕固懷恩出身蕃將世家，掌朔方兵柄多年，廣德初年曾奉命領朔方軍及回紇兵收復被吐蕃攻陷的長安，本是朝廷倚重的藩帥；但宦官魚朝恩等監軍使權力膨脹，屢以他事貶抑河朔將帥，其家族與部曲屢遭清算處置，逼迫他與朝廷徹底決裂。與此同時，唐廷自763年吐蕃陷長安之後對西北邊防始終以「羈縻敷衍」為務：永泰元年正月派四鎮行營節度使馬璘兼南道和蕃使出訪吐蕃，三月十九日吐蕃藉「假意和談」遣使至唐廷刺探軍情，唐代宗竟派宰相元載、杜鴻漸等接待，雙方在興唐寺會盟達致協議，唐廷對即將到來的軍事攻擊毫無戒備，只把河西防務交給幾名節度使虛應故事。這一體制性的鬆懈，恰好與河北叛軍的戰意疊合：僕固懷恩在朔方、河朔軍中仍有大量舊部與被朝廷冷落的將校，他以「奉密詔討吐蕃」為名收攏人心、籌措馬匹與器械，聯絡吐蕃、回紇、党項羌、奴剌、吐谷渾，約定內應而外攻。九月初十前後，聯軍的三路大軍同時發動，唐廷直至邊報連至、叛騎已近才被迫下制親征，戰略上已完全喪失主動。
causeEn: The immediate cause lay in the breakdown between the Hebei military circuits and the centre after the An Lushan rebellion, together with a series of failures in the court's frontier management. Pugu Huai'en came from a family of foreign military origin and had held the Hebei command for many years; early in the Guangde era he had been entrusted with leading the Hebei troops together with Uyghur cavalry to retake Chang'an after the Tibetans had taken it, and was at first a commander the court relied upon. But the supervising eunuchs such as Yu Chao'en grew ever more powerful, repeatedly demoted and sidelined the commanders of the Hebei circuits, and his family and troops were repeatedly purged and punished, driving him into complete rupture with the court. At the same time, after the Tibetans had taken Chang'an in 763, the Tang court's frontier policy in the northwest remained essentially a matter of placating and stalling. In the first month of 765 it sent Ma Lin, commander of the Four Garrisons circuit and also the commissioner for southern and Tibetan affairs, to visit Tibet; on the nineteenth day of the third month the Tibetans, 'pretending to negotiate', sent envoys to the Tang court to spy on its military situation, and Emperor Daizong actually had chancellors Yuan Zai and Du Hongjian receive them, the two sides reaching an agreement at the Xingtang monastery. The court had therefore no guard at all against the military blow that was coming, entrusting the defence of the Hexi corridor to a handful of circuit commanders in name only. This institutional slack coincided exactly with the war fever in the Hebei ranks. Pugu Huai'en still had many old subordinates and disgraced officers in the Hebei and Shaofang armies; using the pretext of 'acting on secret orders to punish the Tibetans' he drew in men and gathered horses and equipment, and made contact with the Tibetans, the Uyghur, the Tangxiang, the Nulüe and the Tuyuhun, arranging for the inside to open while the outside attacked. Around the tenth day of the ninth month the three columns of the coalition moved simultaneously, and it was only as repeated reports of the border came in and rebel horsemen drew near that the court was forced to order a personal campaign. Strategically it had already lost the initiative entirely.
impact: 此役對唐室的意義，一在補上763年陷京之恥未能雪洗的缺口。763年吐蕃入長安、焚府庫而去，使唐廷在西北的威信與物資體系重創，關中數年之後仍處於「吐蕃屢入、邊軍疲於奔命」的循環中；765年這一役則是唐廷首次在關中正面擊退吐蕃聯軍並把其逐回隴右，雖然規模有限，但它向整個西北戰線傳達了一個明確訊號：吐蕃與河北叛軍的聯手並非無懈可擊，關中的城防與騎兵在正確的調度下足以讓進攻方付出代價。對僕固懷恩本人而言，這是一場成敗在此的豪賭：一旦聯軍破長安，他便重開河朔、問鼎中原；如今聯軍崩散，他本人又於十月初九暴死——傳統記載多與其母被誅、舊部受疑等宿怨相繫，無論如何，他一死，這場以藩帥身份主導的叛亂頓時失去核心，河北各部各自為政，再無統一號令，朝廷得以分化招撫，史稱僕固懷恩死後河朔叛勢遂衰。戰略層面，此役也留下了兩份可供後人檢驗的樣本：一份是郭子儀式的「不戰而屈人之兵」——以一杯酒、一封書信分化敵營，讓數十萬聯軍在出擊前先自相殘疑，這在唐代邊事中被反覆援引；另一份是唐廷整體防禦體系的問題，它顯示多節度使分守、缺乏統一指揮與情報協調的防線，在面對協調進攻時處處落後，最終靠一次敵方內部分裂才換來轉機。制度上，唐廷以聯姻、封賞、回紇援軍換取邊境喘息的做法在此後數十年延續，回紇也藉此恢復在漠北的優勢，而吐蕃的攻勢雖然受挫，卻未停止。
impactEn: The significance of this campaign for the Tang lay in one respect above all: it went some way toward making up for the humiliation of the capture of Chang'an in 763, which had shattered the court's prestige and its material system in the northwest and left Guanzhong for years trapped in a cycle of repeated Tibetan incursions and exhausted frontier troops. The campaign of 765 was the first time the Tang court had beaten back a Tibetan coalition in Guanzhong and driven it back towards Longyou. The scale was limited, but it sent an unmistakable signal along the whole northwest front: the alliance of Tibetans and Hebei rebels was not invulnerable, and the cities and cavalry of Guanzhong, properly directed, could make the attacker pay. For Pugu Huai'en it was a desperate gamble in which everything was staked: had the coalition broken into Chang'an he would have re-established himself in Hebei and challenged the centre outright. Instead the coalition collapsed, and he himself died suddenly on the ninth of the tenth month. Traditional accounts connect that death to old grievances — his mother executed, his old subordinates mistrusted — and however the circumstances are read, his death stripped the rebellion of its core. The Hebei formations fell to acting for themselves with no common command, the court was able to divide and conciliate them, and history has it that after Pugu Huai'en's death the Hebei rebel movement declined. At the tactical level the campaign left behind two instructive models. One was Guo Ziyi's style of defeating the enemy without fighting him, breaking up the enemy camp with a cup of wine and a message so that a host of hundreds of thousands fell to quarrelling among themselves before it ever struck; this was repeatedly invoked in Tang frontier writing. The other was the Tang defensive system itself, which showed that a line divided among many circuit commanders, lacking unified command and intelligence coordination, was everywhere on the back foot against a coordinated attack, and that the turning point came only from a split in the enemy. Institutionally, the court's reliance on marriage, enfeoffment and Uyghur auxiliaries to buy breathing space in the frontier continued for decades afterwards; the Uyghur recovered their position in the steppe by the same means, and although the Tibetan offensive was checked it never stopped.
result: 結果是唐軍守住了長安，聯軍三路皆潰。九月廿一日下制親征之後，唐廷以分兵扼守與遊騎襲擾拖住北路吐蕃主力的日程，使其在奉天、醴泉、涇陽三地反覆空耗；十月一日聯軍合兵再攻奉天、初八圍涇陽皆無功而退，北原扎營時傳出僕固懷恩暴死，吐蕃與回紇為爭盟主而內訌，郭子儀乘間遣李光瓚說回紇、並親至其營執酒定約，回紇倒戈，局勢於此逆轉。十月十五日，唐軍在靈台西原追上尚未展開的尚結息部十萬餘人，斬獲極重，唐將白元光率精騎居前衝陣，斬虜甚眾；十月十八日，唐與回紇再在涇州東部合擊，吐蕃主將中箭、軍心大亂，被迫舉營退走，聯軍主力退出關中，轉回隴右、河西。從軍事結果看，唐廷贏得了一場乾淨的防禦反擊：長安未再受威脅，奉天、醴泉、涇陽、靈台一線的城邑得以保全，而吐蕃南路軍與回紇騎兵都受到重創，唐軍並繳獲大量器械、軍旗、馬匹與駱駝。但勝利是有限而昂貴的：叛唐的河北軍主力並未在關中被消滅，僕固懷恩之死只使河朔叛軍失去統一的名號與外藩的支援，黨項羌、吐谷渾仍在關中與河套一帶游鬥，吐蕃的邊疆壓力亦從未解除。763年以來「叛軍為內、蕃軍為外」的戰略此役再度被破解，但破解靠的是敵軍自身的分裂、將領的膽識與外交的手腕，而非結構性的力量對比——這一課此後的河朔與西北戰事都還在補。
resultEn: The result was that the Tang held Chang'an and all three coalition columns broke up. After the order for a personal campaign on the twenty-first day of the ninth month, the court used divided garrisons and harassing light cavalry to hold the northern Tibetan main force to a timetable, wasting it alternately before Fengtian, Liquan and Jingyang. On the first of the tenth month the coalition joined forces and struck Fengtian again, and on the eighth it ringed Jingyang; both attempts failed and it withdrew, and it was while it lay camped on the northern plain that the news of Pugu Huai'en's sudden death reached it. The Tibetans and the Uyghur then fell to quarrelling over who should lead the alliance, and Guo Ziyi seized the moment, sending Li Guangzhan to make contact with the Uyghur and going in person to their camp to seal a pact over wine. The Uyghur turned, and the situation reversed from that point. On the fifteenth of October the Tang caught Shang Jiexi's force of more than 100,000 men before it could deploy on the western plain of Lingtai and destroyed it, with Bai Yuanguang's elite cavalry in the van; on the eighteenth the Tang and the Uyghur struck together again east of Jingzhou, the Tibetan commander was struck by an arrow, the army's morale broke, and it was forced to pull up its camp and leave, the main body of the coalition withdrawing out of Guanzhong towards Longyou and Hexi. Militarily the Tang had won a clean defensive counterstroke: Chang'an was no longer threatened, the county towns along the Fengtian, Liquan, Jingyang and Lingtai line were preserved, and both the southern Tibetan army and the Uyghur cavalry were badly mauled, the Tang recovering large quantities of equipment, standards, horses and camels. But the victory was limited and expensive. The main body of the Hebei rebel army was not destroyed in Guanzhong; Pugu Huai'en's death stripped the Hebei movement of a common banner and of external support rather than of its strength, and the Tangxiang and Tuyuhun continued to operate along the frontier of Guanzhong and Hetao, while the Tibetan pressure was not lifted. The strategic pattern of 'rebel within, Tibetan without' that had marked 763 was broken again, but it was broken through the enemy's own division, the dash of an individual commander and the diplomacy of a single general, not through any structural shift in the balance of power — and that lesson was still being absorbed in the Hebei and northwest campaigns of the decades that followed.
